items.title: feat: kimi-k2 DeepEP v1 + NVSHMEM-over-EFA arm (32-node results) + ep-backend scale limits
items.body:
## Summary

- Adds the **DeepEP v1 + NVSHMEM-over-EFA dispatcher arm** to the `kimi-k2` Megatron-Bridge test case (third arm, mirroring the `qwen3-235b` 3-way pattern) with **measured 32-node results** on literal Kimi-K2 (256× B300, TP8/PP8/EP32) — the parent README's "not yet validated at 16–32 nodes" follow-up is now closed.
- Extends `micro-benchmarks/expert-parallelism/ep-backend-comparison` with a **16/32-node (128/256-rank) scale run**: new NCCL reference numbers plus source-cited documentation of the hard scale limits every DeepEP-class kernel hits past 64–160 ranks.
- Launcher (`run-ab-rawpods.sh`) gains two env-gated, default-off capabilities needed to run on FSx-less local-zone capacity blocks (`STORAGE=hostpath`, `GDRCOPY_DEV=on`) and two bug fixes.

## Changes

### kimi-k2: DeepEP+NVSHMEM arm (`3.test_cases/megatron/megatron-bridge/`)

Measured 2026-07-14 on a 32× `p6-b300.48xlarge` Capacity Block (us-east-1-atl-2a local zone), campaign `20260714T0515Z-k2-nvshmem-pp8-32n-ue1`, image `megatron-bridge-uccl:nemo-26.04.01-deepep-nvshmem-567632d-cu13` (NVSHMEM v3.7.0-0, DeepEP `567632d`, the [`deepep-benchmark`](https://github.com/awslabs/awsome-distributed-ai/tree/main/micro-benchmarks/expert-parallelism/deepep-benchmark) NVSHMEM-over-libfabric/EFA build):

| cell | DeepEP+NVSHMEM (2026-07-14) | UCCL deepep (2026-06-04) | NCCL alltoall (2026-06-04) |
|---|---|---|---|
| mb=4, overlap=on | **3.742 s/iter · 224.6 TF/GPU · 280.2k tok/s** | 3.834 · 219.1 · 273.5k | 5.793 · 144.8 · 181.0k |
| mb=4, overlap=off | 6.632 s/iter · 126.4 TF/GPU | **6.041 · 138.8** | 9.303 · 90.1 |
| mb=1, overlap=off | 13.538 s/iter · 61.9 TF/GPU | 14.98 · 56.0 | **12.88 · 65.1** |

Cross-campaign comparison (different cluster/date/storage than the June UCCL/NCCL A/B) — caveat documented in RESULTS.md. Validity per cell: `Selected provider is efa` on all 32 nodes, 0 stalls, `n_steady` 20/20, `parse-runs.py` transport = nvshmem, iteration-1 loss matches the June arms to 5 significant figures.

- `kimi-k2/README.md`: 3-arm table, NVSHMEM run instructions, `GDRCOPY_DEV` section, "running without FSx (`STORAGE=hostpath`)" section (per-node staging incl. the offline `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3` HF cache the DSV3 recipe scaffolding needs, per-cell harvest loop)
- `kimi-k2/benchmarks/RESULTS.md`: new NVSHMEM section + fixed reproduce block (`ARM` is positional, the old example passed it as env and would not run)
- `README.md` (parent): recommendation bullet updated with the measured 32-node outcome; kimi-k2 models-table row now 3-way

### Launcher (`run-ab-rawpods.sh`) — env-gated, defaults unchanged

- `STORAGE=pvc|hostpath` (+ `FSX_PVC`, `HOSTPATH_ROOT`): the `/fsx` volume source was hard-coded to the `fsx-kimi-k2` PVC; `hostpath` backs it with node-local NVMe for clusters without FSx
- `GDRCOPY_DEV=on`: hostPath-mounts `/dev/gdrdrv` (privileged). NVSHMEM grows its symmetric heap dynamically (CUDA-VMM) once buffers outgrow the 1 GiB init chunk, and registering grown chunks over libfabric/EFA requires GDRCopy **in-container**; on clusters whose nvidia container toolkit ignores `NVIDIA_GDRCOPY=enabled`, every rank dies at `mem_heap.cpp:1361 register_mem_handle failed` without this
- Fix: `set -u` crash on direct invocation (`HF_HOME` default referenced `STAGE` before it was set)
- Fix: `HF_HOME`/`HF_HUB_OFFLINE` were computed but never threaded into the pod env (dead variables)

### ep-backend-comparison: 16/32-node scale run (`micro-benchmarks/expert-parallelism/`)

- `RESULTS.md`: new "32 / 16 nodes — 256 / 128 ranks" section. NCCL alltoall matched-size busbw 73.8 GB/s (128 ranks) / 54.7 GB/s (256 ranks); NVSHMEM HT dispatch tunes to 74.7 GB/s RDMA at 16 nodes. Hard limits (each reproduced ≥2×, source-cited):
  - DeepEP HT: 160-rank cap (`NUM_MAX_NVL_PEERS 8 × NUM_MAX_RDMA_PEERS 20`, `kernels/configs.cuh`); per-node-count template instantiation table; stock combine tuning aborts at 16 RDMA peers (`internode.cu:2363`)
  - UCCL HT: `int32` `num_rdma_bytes` overflow above 64 ranks (`uccl_ep.cc:431`)
  - UCCL LL: `kAtomicBufferSize` signaling-arena overflow at ≥128 ranks (`ep_config.hpp:279`)
  - DeepEP LL over NVSHMEM-libfabric: host-proxy `FI_EAGAIN` retry exhaustion at ≥128 PEs with different victim ranks each run (statistical fan-out limit, not a bad node — verified across 4 runs)
- `README.md`: "Scaling beyond 8 nodes" section (operational guidance incl. the gdrdrv workaround); `env_vars.example` annotated
- Toleration fix: `nccl-alltoall.yaml` and the three `uccl-ep-benchmark` manifests were missing the `workload=bench` toleration the deepep manifests already carry — pods stay `Pending` on tainted B300 pools without it (launcher + worker both patched)

## Test plan

- All three kimi-k2 NVSHMEM cells run end-to-end on real hardware (32× p6-b300) and pass every `parse-runs.py` gate; numbers above are from `index.csv`
- All ep-backend numbers from launcher logs collated with `collect_results.py` and cross-checked against raw logs
- Each documented limit reproduced at least twice; DeepEP/UCCL assert lines quoted verbatim from the shipped sources
- `bash -n run-ab-rawpods.sh` clean; default-path pod rendering unchanged (PVC volume, no privileged, no gdrdrv mount)
- All manifests re-validated as YAML after the toleration patch; relative links in all modified markdown verified to resolve

items.title: Precision/fidelity improvements; restore MSS and VMP2000 benchmark reads
items.body:
> **Stacked on #56** (`improve/perturb-mixing-qc-flags`) → #55 → #54. This PR's base is #56's branch, so the diff shows only the new work. Merge in order, cherry-picking onto fresh main per the squash-merge workflow.

## Summary

This PR completes the remaining future-work items from the stack (with var(ln χ) confirmed out of scope until a published reference exists — none found by either of us). Six precision/fidelity improvements, two honest-documentation items, and one **regression fix the final benchmark sweep caught in our own stack**:

1. **Regression fix:** the `_read_l1` slow-grid temperature interpolation added in #54 crashed on the `(N_TEMP_SENSORS, TIME)` TEMP layout used by MSS Baltic and VMP2000 Faroe Bank, breaking those two benchmark L1 reads. Now fixed and re-verified — and as a bonus those datasets get real per-window viscosity temperature for the first time (they silently used the 10 °C fallback even before the regression).
2. **`ct_align` wraparound:** conductivity was shifted with `np.roll`, splicing one record end into the other (the same defect the FP07 calibration had); now edge-hold, with the canonical `shift_edge_hold` helper moved to `processing/ct_align.py` and reused by `fp07_cal`.
3. **Method-1 chi grid quantization:** the 200-point log-grid search left a ~4.7% quantization on χ — the primary output. A parabolic refinement of the cost minimum (vertex of the parabola through the minimum and its neighbours, in log₁₀χ) reduces synthetic-recovery error to <0.5% for off-grid χ values. Regression test added.
4. **Per-section despike pass counts:** the bit-8 QC flag now uses each window's own section pass count — the benchmark `PASS_COUNT_SH(probe, section)` semantics exactly — replacing the per-channel maximum (which was exact only for single-section profiles). `L2Data` carries per-(channel, section) counts, `L3Data` per-window counts; `_compute_flags` accepts both layouts.
5. **Parabolic detrend (ODAS fidelity):** when Goodman cleaning is not applied, ODAS detrends FFT segments parabolically (`get_diss_odas.m:460`); we used linear everywhere. The no-Goodman branch (in both `scor160/l3.py` and the rsi viewer window path) now uses parabolic; Goodman-cleaned spectra remain linear per `clean_shear_spec.m`. The `_detrend_segment`/`_detrend_batch` machinery already supported it — only the call-site convention was wrong.
6. **Speed-smoothing conflation:** the L2 fall-rate computation pre-smoothed `dP/dt` at `HP_cut` — the **shear high-pass** cutoff, an unrelated parameter — before the 0.68/τ pass. ODAS smooths exactly once at 0.68/τ; that is now the behavior when `speed_tau > 0` (HP_cut survives only as the `speed_tau ≤ 0` fallback, where it is the sole filter). Benchmark speed agreement unchanged to printed precision (RMS 0.0019 m/s), epsilon agreement unchanged — the fix is parameter semantics, not numbers.

Documentation honesty:

7. **FP07 τ pairings:** `fp07_model='double_pole'` auto-pairs with the fixed 3 ms Goto et al. (2016) time constant — it does **not** reproduce Peterson & Fer (2014), who combined a double-pole response with a speed-dependent τ. The docstrings now state the pairings, the provenance of each (τ₀, exponent), and exactly how to reproduce Peterson & Fer (`fp07_double_pole` + `fp07_tau(speed, model='peterson')`).
8. **Iterative chi fit limits:** the docstring claimed both integration limits are refined between iterations; only the lower limit is (k_u is fixed at the last valid wavenumber). Now stated plainly, along with the fact that the 0.04 coefficient in `k_star = 0.04·kB·√(κ/ν)` follows the original implementation and has not been verified against Peterson & Fer's text (paywalled).

## Verification

- **Full benchmark sweep, all six ATOMIX datasets** (this sweep is what caught the regression in item 1):

| Dataset | ε within factor 2 | Method agreement |
|---|---|---|
| VMP250 Tidal | 100% | 96.9% / 100% |
| VMP250 Tidal cs | 96.9–100% | 93.8% / 96.9% |
| MR1000 Minas Passage | 100% (4 probes) | 100% |
| Epsilometer | 100% | 98.9–100% |
| MSS Baltic *(restored)* | 98.1–100% | 100% |
| VMP2000 Faroe Bank *(restored)* | 100% | 100% |

  These match the historical audit values — no degradation from any change in this PR, and the two restored datasets are back to their documented agreement.
- **Flag comparison context** (recorded in the commit): only the VMP250 pair and MR1000 carry the ATOMIX threshold attributes; their flags agree 83–100% exactly. VMP2000 (no attrs) agrees 98.5%; MSS and the Epsilometer carry pre-convention flag metadata with unknown thresholds and differ only on the threshold-sensitive fom/ratio bits — as expected, and not something we can or should tune to.
- **Full suite:** 2,362 passed, 10 skipped (+1 regression test for the 2-D TEMP layout, +1 chi-refinement precision test). `ruff check` + `mypy` clean.

## A note on process

The MSS/VMP2000 regression existed since #54's temperature fix: my post-change benchmark runs covered only the four datasets I was actively comparing, and the empty output for the other two read as "no comparable flags" rather than "crashed." The full six-dataset sweep is now the standard closing check (it is how this PR caught the bug), and the regression test pins the layout that broke.

Ship-the-win: granite4.1:8b becomes the `factual-recall` generator profile pick at the 12 and 8 GB tiers. Balanced default is NOT touched.

| Generator | Strict Qwen judge | Cross-family llama judge | VRAM (q4) | License | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| granite4.1:8b | **54.8** | 60.4 | 4.9 GB | Apache-2.0 | F-016 |
| gemma4:12b (prior 12 GB pick) | 53.8 | **61.4** | ~12 GB | Gemma | N-017 |
| MemOS-lossless (head-to-head) | 54.0 | 61.2 | n/a | n/a | N-017 |
| llama3.1:8b (prior 8 GB pick) | 49.2 | 54.4 | ~5 GB | Llama | E-023 / F-015 |
| qwen3.5:9b (shipped balanced default) | 42.8 | 51.2 | ~6 GB | Apache-2.0 | N-017 |

LoCoMo kill criterion (E-024, pre-registered before results, external qwen3:4b judge, same-config baseline arm): granite4.1:8b **FAILED**, 0.475 vs qwen3.5:9b 0.515 (needed within 0.02). It wins SingleHop (0.679 vs 0.630) but loses Temporal (0.381 vs 0.524) and OpenDomain (0.385 vs 0.538), the same shape gemma4:12b showed. So granite qualifies only for the single-fact-QA profile, never the balanced default.

## What changed per tier (`factual-recall` profile only)

- **gpu-12gb**: gemma4:12b -> granite4.1:8b. Statistical tie on score (54.8/60.4 vs 53.8/61.4); tie broken by 4.9 GB vs 12 GB VRAM (frees room for reranker/embedder co-residency) and Apache-2.0 vs the Gemma license. gemma4:12b stays documented as the prior pick.
- **gpu-8gb**: llama3.1:8b -> granite4.1:8b. Decisive: 54.8/60.4 vs 49.2/54.4 at comparable VRAM, fits 8 GB with headroom.
- **gpu-4gb**: unchanged, llama3.1:8b (granite at 4.9 GB q4 does not fit a 4 GB card).

## What explicitly did NOT change

- The `balanced` default profile (qwen3.5:9b on 12/8 GB, llama3.1:8b on 4 GB) is untouched, per the E-024 kill criterion.
- The 97.0% Recall@5 headline (judge-free) is unaffected.

## Files

- `taosmd/generator_profiles.py`: registry flip + updated evidence/notes (F-016/E-024 cited)

items.title: fix(analyzer): type point and line as tuples on 0.4x, and take the float bounds from the database
items.body:
## A `point` column rejected every row the driver returns

On `drizzle-orm@0.4x`, the major nearly every user runs, the analyzer typed `point` and `line` as
`string`. `packages/analyzer/src/index.ts` had a coarse fallback:

```ts
if (/Point|Line/i.test(ctor)) return { tsType: 'string', dbType: 'TEXT' };
```

So the emitted schema rejected `[1, 2]`, which is what `mapFromDriverValue` returns, and accepted
`"1,2"`, which it never produces. On insert too, where `mapToDriverValue` then received a value it
could not index. The codec path used on v1 got both right, which is why the cross-major diff could
see it.

The database settles it independently of what any validator says:

```
[1,2]  maps to (1,2)   accepted, reads back as [1,2]
"1,2"  maps to (1,,)   Postgres refuses it
```

## The float bounds were `drizzle-zod`'s heuristic, not the column's limit

The same fallback left floats unbounded, so DRZL accepted values official rejected. The obvious fix
was to copy official's bounds. That was wrong, and the first attempt at this shipped it: measured
against a real Postgres, **official's bounds reject values the database stores**.

```
before  probes where Postgres stores the value and both DRZL and official refuse it: 10
after                                                                                  5
        DRZL alone refuses it: 0
```

The five that remain are `Infinity` and `NaN`, described below.

**The bound is now split by dialect, because two databases disagree.** Both edges were found by
bisecting the raw bit pattern of a double against a real server, with values sent as literals so the
server parsed them rather than a driver:

| | edge | doubles above the largest float32 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Postgres `real` | `3.4028235677973366e38` (`2**128 - 2**103`) | 268435456 |
| MySQL 8.4 `FLOAT` | the largest float32 exactly | 0 |

Widening every 4 byte float to Postgres's number would have promised a write MySQL answers
`Out of range value for column` to. `MySqlFloat` and `SingleStoreFloat` keep the narrower bound, now
measured rather than inherited.

That distinction is not academic: the old bound refused `3.4028235e+38`, which is the value a
text-protocol driver hands back for a full-magnitude float4. Refusing what the driver returns is the
same defect as the `point` typing above. A probe for exactly that value is now in both pools, inside
`ALLOWED[pg/c_real]`'s signature and outside `mysql/m_float`'s, so a regression either way fails by
name.

## Measured against the databases

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ground-truth probes | 1400 | 1440 |
| DRZL agrees with Postgres | 1012 | **1048** |
| `drizzle-orm` agrees | 979 | 1013 |
| DRZL closer than `drizzle-orm` | 33 | **35** |
| DRZL further | 0 | **0** |
| JSON Schema agrees | 857 of 1221 | 890 of 1258 |

Ledgers shrank as the defects were fixed: the cross-major map went from 54 fields on 33 columns to
32 on 26, and the 0.4x parity ledger from 22 known-defect columns to 13.

## What stops validating

Stated plainly because this ships. On `drizzle-orm@0.4x` a 4 byte float goes from unbounded to
bounded, so values above the float4 range that validated before are refused now, and `Infinity` is
refused by valibot and arktype where it was accepted before. `NaN` was never accepted by any
generator in any state. The changeset carries the same detail.

## Things this found and did not fix

Each is filed with its measurement rather than carried quietly:

- **Views are invisible to the analyzer on 0.4x**, so every view generates nothing at all.
- **Nothing in the parity comparison is nullable**: 0 of 40 Postgres columns, 0 of 29 MySQL, 0 of 14
  SQLite. Every generator's nullable path is emitted by every run and compared by nothing.
- **Both passes are blind to TypeBox optionality**, in either direction, because the harness reads
  `s.properties[k]` and TypeBox's `Optional` modifier is inert on an extracted property.
- **`point({mode:'xy'})` is typed `string` on both majors**, not only 0.4x. It needs a new
  `ColumnShape`, and no fixture in any gate contains an object-mode column.
- **Cockroach and MSSQL** state `number float` with no codec, so both take MySQL's narrower bound;
  that is wrong for Cockroach. Both dialects already lose whole type families to `unknown`.

## A gate for numbers in the documentation

Four user-facing numbers on this branch turned out to be false, and the fourth was found only after
five review rounds: `docs/guide/benchmarks.md` claimed `DRZL 1007 / closer on 28` for a run printing
1012 and 33. In every case the comment next to the code was right and only the prose away from the
code had drifted.

The benchmarks block is now compared line by line against a log the database stages write. Both
controls run: a fabricated digit fails naming the line, and breaking the anchor fails rather than
passing vacuously. The general case, numbers in prose with nothing behind them, is filed.

## Verification

`pnpm build`, `pnpm -r test` (918 tests across 12 packages), `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`,
`pnpm verify:packed` and `pnpm -C docs build` all pass.

Every control quoted here was run, reverted, and the tree verified byte identical afterwards.

items.title: Rebuild the project into a working, tested and measured system
items.body:
## Summary

The repository did not run. Every entry point failed at import, the test suite could not be collected, and six of the modules that did exist were placeholders returning zeros. This PR makes it work, fixes two algorithmic defects found by measuring the output, and replaces the documentation's fabricated benchmark numbers with real ones.

## What was broken

| File | Problem |
|---|---|
| `src/core/sar_image_processor.py` | Imported `skimage.feature.peak_local_maxima` — no such function (it's `peak_local_max`) |
| `src/__init__.py` | Imported `OilSpillDetector`, `DataVisualizer` and two other modules that were never written |
| `api/main.py` | Called `pd.Timestamp` without importing pandas; mounted a `static/` directory that doesn't exist |
| `main.py` | Imported three modules from a package path that doesn't exist |
| `src/evaluation_metrics.py` and 5 others | Placeholders — `return 0.0`, `return np.zeros_like(image)`, `pass` |

`pytest` failed at collection with `ImportError`. Nothing in the project could execute.

## Two algorithmic defects, found by measuring

**CLAHE was destroying the signal.** It was applied by default and advertised as an improvement. CLAHE equalises contrast *within local tiles*, so a slick wider than a tile has its interior brightened to match the surrounding sea — erasing exactly what detection depends on.

> Mean IoU **0.85 → 0.32**

Contrast enhancement is now off by default for detection, with a test pinning the default so it cannot silently return.

**Local thresholding cannot see a large slick.** Thresholding each pixel against its immediate neighbourhood fails on any slick wider than the window: the local mean sinks with the slick and the contrast cancels, leaving only the rim detected.

> Recall **0.009 → 0.971**

Replaced with a wide-window background estimate and Otsu on the ratio image — under SAR's multiplicative noise model, that ratio is the physically meaningful quantity (≈1.0 over sea, 0.3–0.5 over oil, independent of absolute brightness).

Separately, the fuzzy method had been mistranslated from MATLAB: `imbinarize(Ieval, 0.8)` keeps the *uniform* class, not the edges. That is physically right — oil damps the capillary waves that give the sea its texture, so a slick is smoother than the water around it. Fixing it took that method from IoU 0.004 to 0.941.

## Measured results

12 synthetic 512×512 scenes, seed 42, single CPU core. Reproduce with `python scripts/generate_docs_images.py`.

| Method | IoU | Dice | Precision | Recall | Boundary F1 | Time |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| K-means clustering | **0.943** | **0.970** | 1.000 | 0.943 | 0.482 | 413 ms |
| Fuzzy edge detection | 0.941 | 0.969 | 0.987 | 0.953 | 0.733 | 149 ms |
| Adaptive threshold | 0.902 | 0.941 | 0.929 | **0.971** | **0.875** | **141 ms** |
| Superpixel clustering | 0.859 | 0.924 | 0.982 | 0.875 | 0.287 | 265 ms |

These are **synthetic** benchmarks. They are a fair comparison between methods and a solid regression test, but they do not predict accuracy on real Sentinel-1 imagery, where look-alikes (low-wind cells, biogenic films, rain cells) are genuinely dark and genuinely smooth. The README says so explicitly.

## Changes

**Structure** — src-layout package (`src/sar_oil_spill/`) installable via `pyproject.toml`, with a `sar-oil-spill` console script. MATLAB sources moved to `matlab/` unchanged.

**Implementations** — the four classical methods ported from MATLAB; full metrics (IoU, Dice, boundary F1, Hausdorff, object-level detection rates); the detection pipeline; the figure generator; an attention-gated U-Net behind an optional `dl` extra.

**Synthetic SAR generator** — Gamma speckle, dB-specified slick damping, swath wind gradient, land. The original dataset is not distributable, which is why nobody could previously run this; now `sar-oil-spill demo` works on a clean clone, and it's what the tests and figures are built on.

**Performance** — the Lee filter was looping over 262,144 pixels per scene in Python; now vectorised over separable box filters, so cost is independent of window size. The fuzzy inference system is evaluated in closed form rather than row-by-row through `evalfis`.

**Service** — FastAPI rewritten on `lifespan`, CPU work moved off the event loop via `asyncio.to_thread`, upload size/extension limits, bounded job registry, correct multipart form parsing. Streamlit app moved off the removed `st.cache` and `use_column_width`.

**Infrastructure** — 165 tests (84% coverage), ruff clean, CI across Python 3.10–3.13 plus a base-dependency smoke job that verifies the package works without the optional extras, non-root multi-stage Dockerfile, `LICENSE`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

**Documentation** — README rewritten against measured output, with 8 generated figures. The previous version advertised IoU 0.847, "10x performance" and 91% test coverage with per-module breakdowns, for code that could not execute; it also documented a directory structure that did not match the tree. Limitations are now stated plainly: synthetic results, no look-alike handling, no georeferencing, no trained model.

Removed `deployment/vercel.json` — the dependency set (OpenCV, SciPy, scikit-image, scikit-learn) exceeds Vercel's serverless bundle limit, so that configuration could never have deployed. `deployment/README.md` explains why.

## Verification

```
165 passed in 8.64s
ruff check .  →  All checks passed!
```

Also verified by hand: the demo, detect, benchmark and dataset CLI commands; the API via `TestClient` (all endpoints); every generated figure inspected visually; all YAML/JSON configs parse; all internal doc links resolve.

**Not verified: the Docker build.** No Docker daemon was available in the environment where this was developed. The `Dockerfile` and the CI job that builds it are written but untested — the CI run on this PR will be the first real exercise of them.

## Review notes

Several defaults look wrong until you know why, and each is explained in a comment or docstring with a test pinning it:

- contrast enhancement disabled (`config.py`)
- background window of 251 px (`traditional_segmentation.py`)
- the fuzzy method thresholding uniformity rather than edges

`remove_small_components` is implemented on `scipy.ndimage` rather than `skimage.morphology.remove_small_objects` because that function renamed `min_size` → `max_size` in scikit-image 0.26 *and* flipped from a strict to an inclusive comparison; doing the count directly keeps one behaviour across supported versions.

items.body:
## What I did

Docgen is the step that reads a component's props and turns them into the `argTypes` behind Controls and the docs page. We are replacing those engines, so we need to know what the old and the new ones actually cost. This note is the contract for measuring that, before any of the measuring code lands.

It fixes four things: which metrics we record, how we make a run repeatable, what shape a budget may take, and which CI tier gates.

## Checklist for Contributors

### Testing

#### The changes in this PR are covered in the following automated tests:

- [ ] stories
- [ ] unit tests
- [ ] integration tests
- [ ] end-to-end tests

#### Manual testing

No manual test is possible or needed — this PR adds one Markdown file and no code.
What it needs instead is a read: does the approach hold up? I would especially like a second opinion on the "not like-for-like" rule, since it decides which numbers we are ever allowed to gate on.

### Documentation

- [x] Add or update documentation reflecting your changes

## Checklist for Maintainers

- [ ] When this PR is ready for testing, make sure to add `ci:normal`, `ci:merged` or `ci:daily` GH label to it to run a specific set of sandboxes. The particular set of sandboxes can be found in `code/lib/cli-storybook/src/sandbox-templates.ts`
- [ ] Declare whether manual QA will be needed for this PR during the next release, through `qa:needed` or `qa:skip`

items.body:
- constants.py: Fix percentile key format in ENDPOINTS_MAPPINGS — the endpoints JSON uses float-format keys (e.g. "99.0") but the mappings used integer strings ("99"), causing latency_check to receive None and crash on the comparison. Updated all latency/ttft/tpot percentile keys to use the .0 suffix (50.0, 90.0, 95.0, 99.0).

items.title: Add security and performance engineers, incident playbook
items.body:
## Summary
Expands the AI engineering team with two new specialist agents and supporting infrastructure for production incident response. Adds the Security Engineer and Performance Engineer roles, a production incident playbook, and reusable skills for security review and query optimization.

## Key changes

- **New agents:**
  - `security-engineer.md` — owns authentication, authorization, secret management, input validation, and OWASP-class risks; reviews changes for security impact and gates high-severity findings as blockers
  - `performance-engineer.md` — owns query optimization, caching, profiling, and benchmarking; diagnoses and fixes hot paths from measured evidence, never speculation

- **New playbook:**
  - `production_incident.md` — end-to-end workflow for production incidents: triage → diagnose → fix → verify → resolve → postmortem; emphasizes stabilization first, evidence-based diagnosis, minimal fixes, and objective verification before declaring done

- **New reusable skills:**
  - `security-review/SKILL.md` — procedure for reviewing changes for security risk, classifying findings by severity (critical/high/medium/low), and producing a PASS/CHANGES REQUIRED verdict
  - `optimize-query/SKILL.md` — procedure for diagnosing and fixing slow queries: measure baseline, inspect actual plan, identify cause, apply minimal fix, re-measure, and report before/after numbers

- **Updated documentation:**
  - `organization.md` — adds Security Engineer and Performance Engineer to the team roster
  - `roadmap.md` — updates team roadmap to reflect security and performance agents as now active (not planned), and clarifies remaining planned additions
  - `README.md` — updates directory structure to show new agents and skills

## Implementation details

- Both new agents follow the established pattern: read organization docs first, check memory for prior decisions, reason from actual code/evidence, and report plainly on what was verified and any residual risk
- Security Engineer gates critical/high findings as hard stops; Performance Engineer requires before/after measurements to prove any optimization
- Incident playbook assigns each step to a specific role (Conductor, specialist, QA) and defines clear outputs; emphasizes that "done" means production is healthy, QA has verified the fix, and a postmortem with recurrence prevention is written
- Both skills are identity-agnostic and reusable by any agent with appropriate access

items.title: perf: Signal alignment vectorization — 80× speedup
items.body:
## Summary

- Vectorize signal alignment and bar execution loop data access, achieving ~80× speedup for the critical path
- Replace per-symbol pandas `reindex` with numpy `searchsorted` + direct array fill
- Pre-extract `.values` arrays in `_execute_bars()` to eliminate per-bar DataFrame hash lookups

## Why

The `_align()` method was the #1 bottleneck in backtest execution, taking ~2-2.5s for 5000 bars × 50 symbols due to repeated pandas `reindex` calls. This made iterative strategy development painfully slow.

Closes #697

## Changes

### `agent/backtest/engines/base.py`
- Rewrite `_align()`: numpy `searchsorted` + direct array fill (replaces per-symbol `reindex`)
- Add `_ffill_1d`/`_ffill_2d` helpers (pure numpy forward-fill with limit)
- `_execute_bars()`: pre-extract `.values` arrays with explicit column ordering, replace `.at[ts, c]` with `array[i, j]`
- `_safe_price()`: keyword-only fast-path params `_arr`/`_row`/`_col`
- `_calc_open_equity()`: use instance-level cached arrays via `getattr`
- Fix column ordering bug: `target_pos.values` and `close_df.values` now use explicit `[codes]` reindexing to guarantee array column order matches the `_code_to_col` mapping

### `agent/tests/test_signal_alignment_perf.py` (new)
- 17 regression tests covering correctness, performance, and integration
- Performance gate: 5000 bars × 50 symbols < 35ms

## Benchmark Results

Environment: Python 3.12, numpy 2.x, pandas 2.x

| Scenario | Before (pandas) | After (numpy) | Speedup |
|----------|----------------|---------------|---------|
| `_align()` 5000 bars × 50 symbols | ~2.0-2.5s | 30ms median | **~80×** |
| `_execute_bars()` per-bar access | ~150μs/bar (DataFrame.at) | ~2μs/bar (array indexing) | **~75×** |
| `_safe_price()` hot path | ~1.5μs/call (hash lookup) | ~50ns/call (direct index) | **~30×** |

Methodology: `time.perf_counter()`, 7 iterations, median reported. Synthetic data: random walk close prices, random signals, 5% NaN gaps.

items.title: Reified generics for PHP, monomorphized through Z-Engine
items.body:
Reified generics for PHP, built on the class-entry specialization API in z-engine.

`Box::of('int')` returns a real, registered class whose property, parameter and return types are `int` — enforced by the engine itself, not by a userland check:

```php
/** @template T */
#[TemplateParameter('T')]
final class Box implements GenericObject
{
    use GenericTemplate;

    private ?T $value = null;

    public function set(T $value): void { $this->value = $value; }
}

$box = new (Box::of('int'))();
$box->set(42);       // fine
$box->set('nope');   // TypeError: Box<int>::set(): Argument #1 ($value) must be of type int
get_class($box);     // "Box<int>"
```

## Status

- [x] **M0** — scaffolding, quality gates, CI
- [x] **M1** — walking skeleton: templates specialize end to end
- [x] **M2** — type-argument grammar, nested generics, bounds, validation
- [x] **M5** — upstream z-engine slot-addressed substitution (lisachenko/z-engine#128, merged)
- [x] **M6** — attribute form (`#[Of]` / `#[OfReturn]`)
- [x] **M7** — benchmark harness and published monomorphization numbers
- [x] **M8** — full design documentation, decisions pinned in AGENTS.md
- [ ] **M3** — identity helpers, autoloader, name parsing
- [ ] **M4** — PHPStan extension and stub generator

## The result this repository exists for

The compile-time generics discussions stall on the assumption that **monomorphization costs a copy of the code per instantiation**. Here it does not, because the specialized class entry shares its method bodies with the template through the engine's own op_array refcount.

Measured, not argued — a 32-method template, specialized 100 times:

| Statements per method | Opcodes per method | Specialize | Codegen (emit + compile) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 12 | 34,448 bytes | 22,480 bytes |
| 200 | 208 | **34,448 bytes** | 399,312 bytes |

The same number to the byte across a 50x change in body size. Note the honest half of it: below about a dozen opcodes per method the class entry's fixed cost makes the copy the *more* expensive of the two. Sharing bodies only pays once there is a body worth sharing.

The one shape that does scale with body size is a `mixed` **parameter** — the only slot that has to un-share the method's opcode array, for the reason in the next section.

Full tables, environment and statistics in `docs/benchmarks.md`, generated by `composer bench`. Every sentence under a table is computed from that run, so a result that moves cannot leave a stale conclusion behind it.

## Where the engine actually keeps a type check

**Rewriting a type and having it enforced are not the same thing.** Which one you get depends on where the check lives:

| Slot | Where the check reads its type | To re-type it |
|---|---|---|
| Property | `zend_property_info`, on every write | rewrite the type |
| Return type | `arg_info[-1]`, read by a `ZEND_VERIFY_RETURN_TYPE` opline | rewrite the type — **if** such an opline exists |
| Parameter, `RECV_INIT` / `RECV_VARIADIC` | `arg_info`, on every call | rewrite the type |
| Parameter, plain `ZEND_RECV` | a type mask the compiler **cached into the opline** | rewrite the type **and** patch the cached mask |

`ZEND_RECV`'s `op2.num` is a verbatim copy of `arg_info.type.type_mask`, upper flag bits included — which is why rewriting `arg_info` alone was invisible at run time, and why patching it means un-sharing that method's opcodes. lisachenko/z-engine#129 does this, with `IS_CONST` operand relocation verified under `zend.assertions=1`.

> An earlier revision of this PR claimed builtin parameters *and return types* could never be enforced. That was wrong for return types, and wrong in general — it came from probing with `return 'x';`, a literal the compiler had already proved, so there was no check opline to observe. Only two cases genuinely remain unreachable: a `mixed` return type, and a return the compiler proved valid. Both are detected up front and rejected rather than silently unenforced.

## A measured non-parity

Dispatch, class-typed parameters and builtin-typed property writes are all at parity with hand-written compiled classes. A **class-typed property write is ~2.3x**, and its cost scales with the length of the type argument's class name while a compiled class stays flat.

Cost that tracks name length is a name being resolved on every write where a compiled class resolves it once. The engine reaches its fast path through a class-entry cache carried on interned strings, and the name z-engine writes into a substituted type is created at run time — that is the first place to look, recorded as a hypothesis rather than a result. It is worst for nested generics, whose type argument names are long by construction.

Reported rather than explained away; the scenario that found it is the one whose prose is generated from its own numbers.

## Two template forms

**Placeholder form** — the slot declares the type parameter as its native type (`private ?T $value`).

**Attribute form** — `#[Of('T')] private mixed $value`. The only way to re-type a `mixed` property, since `mixed` has no type name for the engine to key on, and (since #129) it reaches `mixed` parameters too.

Both may be mixed in one class; the strategies contribute to a shared plan rather than being selected between.

## Other decisions worth reviewing

**Angle brackets in the mangled name are load-bearing.** No PHP source can declare a class containing `<` and no PSR-4 autoloader can resolve one, so a specialization can never collide with a real class — while `get_class()` and stack traces stay readable. `Box<Box<int>>` nests naturally.

**The cache adopts rather than fails.** A specialized name already in the class table is recorded and returned; without this a second factory instance or a boot-time warm-up would collide.

**Attributes are the runtime source of truth, never doc comments.** `opcache.save_comments=0` makes `doc_comment` NULL. The `tests-opcache` CI job runs the whole suite that way as a permanent guard.

**Nullable type arguments are refused.** Substitution preserves the template's declared nullability and cannot add it, so `Box<?int>` would quietly produce a non-nullable slot.

**A specialization is a sibling, not a subclass** — `$box instanceof Box` is `false`. Not fixable, so `GenericObject` is a required marker and there is an explicit test asserting the behaviour.

## Verification

`composer test` — 60 tests, 226 assertions, green; also green under `opcache.enable_cli=1 opcache.save_comments=0` (1 documented skip: a `mixed` parameter whose body is opcache-shared puts its literals out of 32-bit reach).
`composer phpstan` — level max over `src`, `tests` and `benchmarks`, no errors, no baseline.
`composer cs:check` — clean.
`composer bench:smoke` — every scenario at its smallest size, asserted for shape and never for a number.

items.title: Experimental: Additional performance improvements as per the optimizations guides
items.body:
# Performance Improvements — `feat/performance-improvements`

**Branch:** `feat/performance-improvements`  
**Base:** `master` at `484b991`  
**Go version:** `go1.26.4` (required; documented in README and CONTRIBUTING.md)  
**Date:** 2026-06-10 → 2026-06-16  
**Commits:** 32 commits ahead of `master`  
**Scope:** 197 files changed, ~14,038 insertions, ~1,644 deletions  
**Release:** v6.0.0 prep included (`gopdfsuit/v6`, pypdfsuit 6.0.0)

---

## Summary

This PR is a profile-driven performance program for gopdfsuit spanning the PDF generation engine, HTTP handlers, signing path, benchmark harnesses, test validation, and release/CI hardening. Work was guided by optimization reports under `guides/optimizations/` plus a cross-stack benchmark validation (`guides/BENCHMARK_COMPARISON_2026-06-15.md`). The program moved from a `master` micro-benchmark baseline through SlopGuard remediation, GoPDFKit parity, Gin HTTP saturation, Zerodha end-to-end throughput targets, cache-bounds/memory stability, tagged-PDF allocation reduction, veraPDF compliance validation, and v6 release prep.

**Headline outcomes:**

| Surface | Baseline | Current (best measured) | Improvement |
|---------|----------|-------------------------|-------------|
| `BenchmarkGoPdfSuit` (internal/pdf) | 26.0 ms/op, 25.6 MB/op | 23.0 ms/op, 21.5 MB/op | **−11.6% latency, −16% alloc** |
| GoPDFKit compare harness (7 workloads) | gopdflib wins 5/7 | **gopdflib wins 7/7** | Up to **+788%** on `png_rows_60` (Jun 15 re-run) |
| Gin HTTP weighted (`tagged_ecdsa`) | ~593 req/s | **~910–1,232 req/s** (run-dependent) | **+54–108%** vs pre-opt; ≥1,000 gate ✅ |
| Gin HTTP post-60399e1 (2-run mean) | 916.8 req/s | **1,025.7 req/s** | **+11.9%** in same session |
| Gin HTTP retail-only | — | **~3,965 req/s** | ≥1,500 gate ✅ |
| Zerodha in-process weighted (48 workers) | ~573 ops/s (Go 1.24) | **~2,646 avg / 2,898 peak ops/s** | **+362% vs 1.24 gold std** (10-run validated) |
| Zerodha retail single-doc (GoPDFSuit) | — | **~1,978 avg / 2,234 peak ops/s** | 10-run validated |
| vs Gotenberg (same k6 harness) | — | **~89× faster** | 910 vs 10 req/s |
| SlopGuard actionable findings | 218 open | **218 fixed** | 100% remediation |
| `make test` compliance gate | go test + pytest | **+ veraPDF post-test validation** | PDF/A-4 + PDF/UA-2 for editor outputs |

> **Throughput variance note:** Gin k6 results vary with system load and run order. Phase 11 peak was **1,232 req/s**; post-revert baseline **1,054 req/s**; June 14 optimization session ended at **1,025.7 req/s** (2-run mean, best run **1,052.7**); June 15 full-suite dedicated k6 validation averaged **910 req/s** (peak **973**). Cite run conditions when comparing numbers.

---

## Source documentation (added or updated on this branch)

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| [`20260610_master_performance_execution_plan.md`](../20260610_master_performance_execution_plan.md) | Master plan: Phase 1 buffer/compression wins, Phase 2 structure-tree pressure |
| [`20260610_phase2_pprof_report.md`](../20260610_phase2_pprof_report.md) | Post-Phase-2 pprof: remaining `fmt.Sprintf`, `drawTable`, compression hotspots |
| [`slopguard-findings.md`](../slopguard-findings.md) | 226 SlopGuard findings; 218 actionable PERF items tracked to completion |
| [`20260610_slopguard_fixes_report.md`](../20260610_slopguard_fixes_report.md) | SlopGuard fix validation via GoPDFKit compare harness (10-run avg) |
| [`20260610_gopdfkit_compare_results.md`](../20260610_gopdfkit_compare_results.md) | Iterative gopdflib vs GoPDFKit comparison through multiple optimization passes |
| [`20260611_gopdfkit_fixed_compare_results.md`](../20260611_gopdfkit_fixed_compare_results.md) | Fixed stub `gopdfkit` module; definitive 7/7 gopdflib wins |
| [`20260611_gin_1500_ops_pprof_report.md`](../20260611_gin_1500_ops_pprof_report.md) | Gin HTTP path to 1,000+ req/s (Phases 0–12, k6 + pprof) |
| [`20260611_zerodha_3000_ops_pprof_report.md`](../20260611_zerodha_3000_ops_pprof_report.md) | Zerodha harness path to 3,000 ops/s (Phases A–G) |
| [`20260611_zerodha_gold_standard_benchmark.md`](../20260611_zerodha_gold_standard_benchmark.md) | Gold-standard 80/15/5 workload on Go 1.26.4 vs Go 1.24 |
| [`20260614_remaining_optimizations_checklist.md`](../20260614_remaining_optimizations_checklist.md) | **New (eb1b2c1)** — cache bounds, structure writer, allocation churn follow-ups; updated through 60399e1 |
| [`../../BENCHMARK_COMPARISON_2026-06-15.md`](../../BENCHMARK_COMPARISON_2026-06-15.md) | **New (d50dfd3)** — cross-stack benchmark validation (10-run Zerodha, k6, GoPDFKit, Gotenberg) |
| [`../../release-prep.md`](../../release-prep.md) | **New (925a691)** — v6 release checklist (version bump, lint, mocks, PyPI, Docker smoke) |

---

## Implementation phases

### Phase 1 — PDF engine buffer & compression (execution plan)

**Source:** `20260610_master_performance_execution_plan.md`

Profiled hotspots on `go1.26.4`: `bytes.growSlice` (21%), `compress/flate.NewWriter` (20%), `slices.Clone` (7%), `BeginMarkedContentBuf` (5%).

**Implemented:**

- Increased pooled final PDF buffer capacity
- Removed extra scratch-slice hop at final assembly; single caller-owned clone
- Stream page content directly into zlib writer (no `contentStream.Bytes()`)
- Replaced `append([]byte(nil), ...)` with explicit `slices.Clone`
- Pre-sized initial page content streams from template complexity

**Results vs `master` baseline:**

| Benchmark | Baseline ns/op | Phase 1 ns/op | Δ |
|-----------|---------------:|--------------:|---|
| `BenchmarkGoPdfSuit` | 26,047,411 | 23,531,821 | **−9.7%** |
| `BenchmarkGenerateTemplatePDF/Rows2000` | 28,903,973 | 24,053,195 | **−16.8%** |

### Phase 2 — Structure tree & table pressure

**Source:** `20260610_master_performance_execution_plan.md`, `20260610_phase2_pprof_report.md`

**Implemented:**

- `StructureManager` page-index maps → slices (`NextMCID`, `ParentTree`)
- `BeginStructureElementCap` for known table/row child counts
- Pre-grew XMP metadata builders
- Annotation object IDs stored on Link structure elements (avoid reverse scans)

**Results (cumulative vs original `master`):**

| Benchmark | Baseline | Post-Phase-2 | Δ |
|-----------|----------|--------------|---|
| `BenchmarkGoPdfSuit` | 26.0 ms, 25.6 MB | 23.0 ms, 21.5 MB | **−11.6% ns, −16% B** |
| `BenchmarkGenerateTemplatePDF/Rows2000` | 28.9 ms, 24.7 MB | 23.8 ms, 22.5 MB | **−17.5% ns, −9% B** |
| allocs/op | ~163,386 | ~157,268 | **−3.7%** |

**Remaining (documented, partially addressed in later commits):** hot-path `fmt.Sprintf` in structure serialization, page content-buffer reuse, `drawTable` / `GetTextWidth` pressure.

### Phase 3 — SlopGuard remediation (218 findings)

**Source:** `slopguard-findings.md`, `20260610_slopguard_fixes_report.md`

**Scope:** 226 exported findings; 8 CWE-only excluded; **218 actionable PERF items fixed** across P1–P6 batches.

**Pattern categories addressed:**

| Rule family | Count (approx) | Representative fix |
|-------------|----------------|--------------------|
| PERF-1 | 20+ | Hoist regex compilation to package-level vars (`xfdf.go`, `merge.go`) |
| PERF-6 / PERF-35 | 50+ | `fmt.Sprintf` → `strconv.AppendInt`, `strings.Builder`, `errors.New` |
| PERF-15 | 30+ | `strconv.Itoa` → `strconv.AppendInt` with scratch buffers |
| PERF-31 | 13 | Remove `defer` from font registry hot path; explicit unlock |
| PERF-32 | 40+ | Eliminate redundant `string`/`[]byte` conversions; `unsafe.Slice` where safe |
| PERF-41/43 | — | `gin.CustomRecovery`; non-blocking stderr logging |
| PERF-46/48 | — | Cheap guards before `TrimSpace` / `bytes.Equal` |
| PERF-4 | — | Map pre-sizing; hoisted `visited` map with `clear()` reuse |

**Validation (GoPDFKit compare harness, 10-run avg):**

| Workload | Before pdf/s | After pdf/s | Δ |
|----------|-------------:|------------:|---|
| `text_240_lines` | 15,994 | **17,434** | **+9.0%** |
| `table_180_rows` | 11,548 | **13,051** | **+13.0%** |
| `table_900_rows` | 2,563 | **2,680** | **+4.6%** |

### Phase 4 — GoPDFKit comparison & deep engine wins

**Source:** `20260610_gopdfkit_compare_results.md`, `20260611_gopdfkit_fixed_compare_results.md`

**Key engine changes across iterative passes:**

- Pooled page content stream buffers; fairer compare harness (cached templates)
- `drawTable`: font-ref cache per cell, standard-font subset skip, precomputed text widths
- Image dedup: shared XObject per repeated cell PNG
- `GeneratePDFBorrowed` / `Release()` — skip final `slices.Clone` on hot path
- `DecodeImageData` MRU fast path; `crypto/md5` → `crypto/sha256` for document-ID hash
- `drawTable` border fast path (uniform borders → single `re S`)
- PDF/UA-2 Table→TR→TD hierarchy restored (no batch-MC shortcut on TR)

**GoPDFKit harness fix:** `replace github.com/cssbruno/gopdfkit` pointed at `/tmp/gopdfkit` stub (empty PDF). Redirected to real `v0.5.2` module.

**Final comparison (3-run median, fixed harness):**

| Workload | GoPDFKit pdf/s | gopdflib pdf/s | Winner | Δ |
|----------|---------------:|---------------:|--------|---|
| `text_short` | 106,256 | 160,863 | gopdflib | +51% |
| `text_240_lines` | 12,034 | 16,810 | gopdflib | +40% |
| `table_180_rows` | 9,237 | 21,023 | gopdflib | +128% |
| `table_900_rows` | 2,081 | 4,338 | gopdflib | +108% |
| `invoice_40_rows` | 32,173 | 71,920 | gopdflib | +124% |
| `png_table_180_rows` | 5,885 | 19,843 | gopdflib | +237% |
| `png_rows_60` | 4,028 | 30,018 | gopdflib | +645% |

**Post PDF/UA-2 TD fix re-run (2-run mean):** gopdflib still **7/7**, with **+27–86%** throughput vs morning run.

**June 15 re-run (`guides/BENCHMARK_COMPARISON_2026-06-15.md`):**

| Workload | GoPDFKit pdf/s | gopdflib pdf/s | Lead |
|----------|---------------:|---------------:|-----:|
| `text_short` | 114,825 | **206,298** | +80% |
| `text_240_lines` | 14,077 | **23,741** | +69% |
| `table_180_rows` | 11,307 | **28,870** | +155% |
| `table_900_rows` | 2,460 | **7,621** | +210% |
| `invoice_40_rows` | 39,240 | **105,514** | +169% |
| `png_table_180_rows` | 6,949 | **32,077** | +362% |
| `png_rows_60` | 4,792 | **42,548** | +788% |

### Phase 5 — Gin HTTP path to 1,000+ req/s

**Source:** `20260611_gin_1500_ops_pprof_report.md`

**Endpoint:** `POST /api/v1/generate/template-pdf`  
**Workload:** 80% retail / 15% active / 5% HFT, PDF/A + tagged + ECDSA signed

| Milestone | Throughput | Median | p99 |
|-----------|----------:|-------:|----:|
| Baseline (pre-opt) | ~593 req/s | 25.6 ms | 563 ms |
| Phase 7 peak | **1,118 req/s** | 16.2 ms | 208 ms |
| Phase 11 peak | **1,232 req/s** | 12.6 ms | 126 ms |
| Post-P12-revert baseline | **1,054 req/s** | 15.5 ms | 143 ms |
| Retail-only | **3,965 req/s** | 7.8 ms | 29 ms |

**Phases implemented (0–11):**

| Phase | Focus | Key changes |
|-------|-------|-------------|
| 0–1 | Harness + concurrency | k6 pprof load test, `MAX_CONCURRENT=48`, `GOMAXPROCS=24` |
| 2 | Signing | ECDSA P-256 default; RSA eliminated from CPU top |
| 3 | JSON ingress | Sonic stream decode, `PreallocForDecode`, `GenerateTemplatePDFBorrowed` |
| 4 | PDF hot path | Struct tree pooling, compress cache bounds, `drawTable` HFT fast path |
| 5 | Saturation | `GIN_FAST_API=1`, `BENCH_MODE` adaptive concurrency |
| 7 | 1,000 gate | Pretouch, tier prealloc, direct struct write, batch MC, HFT deferral, buffer grow, page striping |
| 8–9 | Decode + draw | Pooled sonic unmarshal, bulk ParentTree, `drawSharedDeferRow` |
| 10–11 | HFT ultra-fast | Split HFT decode (`hft_decode.go`), flate single-pass >32 KiB |
| 12 | ❌ Reverted | CRC32 fingerprint, in-place sig hex, store-uncompressed — no E2E gain |

**Primary files:** `cmd/gopdfsuit/main.go`, `internal/handlers/handlers.go`, `json_decode.go`, `hft_decode.go`, `internal/pdf/generator.go`, `draw.go`, `structure.go`, `compress_cache.go`, `makefile` (`load-pprof`, `load-pprof-1k`, `load-pprof-1500`)

### Phase 6 — Zerodha harness path to 3,000 ops/s

**Source:** `20260611_zerodha_3000_ops_pprof_report.md`, `20260611_zerodha_gold_standard_benchmark.md`

**Harness:** `sampledata/gopdflib/zerodha/main.go` — 5,000 iterations, 48 workers, 80/15/5 mix

| Milestone | Peak ops/s | 5-run avg | Avg latency |
|-----------|----------:|----------:|------------:|
| Pre-opt (RSA, Go 1.24 gold std) | — | **573 ops/s** | 80.7 ms |
| Go 1.26.4 gold std (3-run median) | — | **1,135 ops/s** | 41.3 ms |
| Post-A7 (ECDSA) | 2,701 | 2,520 | ~17 ms |
| Post Phase F + G2 (full regen) | **2,751** | **2,476** | ~18.9 ms |
| **June 15 10-run validation** | **2,898** | **2,646** | 17.7 ms |

**Phases implemented:**

| Phase | Focus | Status |
|-------|-------|--------|
| A | Signature fast path | ✅ PEM/signer cache, in-place embed, ECDSA P-256 |
| B | Concurrency | ✅ 48 workers, `GOMAXPROCS=24`, seeded 80/15/5 schedule |
| C | Compression | ✅ Flate pool, store-uncompressed threshold, page compress cache (G2) |
| D | Allocation | ✅ `GeneratePDFBorrowed`, structure MCID batch, font registry pool |
| E | Harness | ✅ `BENCH_SEED`, `BENCH_SKIP_WRITE`, per-worker stats |
| F | Post-pprof fixes | ✅ F1–F4, C4–C6 (buffer estimate, subset cache, textTjBuf) |
| G3 | Parallel struct tree | ❌ Reverted (~60% regression on HFT) |
| G4 | Template PDF cache | ❌ Removed (misleading benchmark; each request must be unique) |

**3000 ops/s target:** Not yet reached (~8% below peak at Phase F). June 15 10-run validation shows sustained **~2,500–2,900 ops/s** (cold single-run outlier was 1,321). Dominant costs: HFT `drawTable` + zlib (~40% CPU from 5% of jobs), retail ECDSA signing.

### Phase 7 — Cache bounds & structure-tree writer (`eb1b2c1`, 2026-06-14)

**Source:** `20260614_remaining_optimizations_checklist.md`  
**Commit:** `eb1b2c1 perf(pdf): bound unbounded caches, optimize structure-tree writer`  
**Note:** This commit also created this PR description file and the remaining-optimizations checklist.

**Problem:** Three `sync.Map`-backed caches could grow without limit on long-lived pods. Structure-tree serialization (`formatStructElemObjectTo`) was still allocating per integer and per Title/Alt field. A pre-session 5-run k6 regression had dropped to **825 req/s** mean (peak 859).

#### HI-2 — Bound previously unbounded caches

| Cache | File | Max entries | Clear API |
|-------|------|-------------|-----------|
| `subsetCache` (font subsets) | `font/subset_cache.go` | **1024** | `ClearSubsetCache()` |
| `imgCache` (decoded images) | `image.go` | **256** | `ResetImageCache()` |
| `propsCache` (parsed prop strings) | `utils.go` | **8192** | `ClearPropsCache()` |

Overflow semantics: full map clear + counter reset (same pattern as `compress_cache.go`).

**New tests:** `subset_cache_test.go`, `image_cache_test.go`, `props_cache_test.go`.

#### MI-3 + MI-1 (partial) — Structure-tree writer allocation cleanup

In `generator.go` (`formatStructElemObjectTo`, `appendObjRefToWriter`):

- **Integers:** `strconv.Itoa` + `WriteString` → `strconv.AppendInt` into stack `[24]byte` + `Write([]byte)`
- **Title/Alt text:** `escapeText(s)` + `WriteString` → `appendEscapedPDFLiteral(scratch[:0], s)` into stack `[1024]byte` (heap fallback if escaped output exceeds 1024 bytes)

**Benchmark (`make bench-k6`, 48 VUs × 35s, weighted `tagged_ecdsa`):**

| Metric | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| 5-run mean | **825 req/s** | **1,006 req/s** (+22%) |
| Peak run | 859 req/s | **1,041 req/s** |
| p99 | ~347 ms | **~270 ms** |

#### Experiments tried and reverted in this session (documented, not shipped)

| Experiment | Result |
|------------|--------|
| HI-3 — larger buffer estimates + pool retention caps (8 MB / 1 MB) | 993 → 962 req/s; `bytes.growSlice` in-use 256 → 338 MB |
| MI-1 — generic `formatStructElemObjectToGeneric[T]()` | 998 → 916 req/s (Go shape-based dispatch) |
| EW-2 — `Load` before `Store` in `storePageCompressEntry` | Single run 808 req/s; HFT latency ~461 ms |

### Phase 7 (continued) — Tagged-PDF allocation churn (`60399e1`, 2026-06-14)

**Source:** `20260614_remaining_optimizations_checklist.md`  
**Commit:** `60399e1 perf: reduce tagged-pdf allocation churn and refresh benchmark evidence`

Four allocation-focused passes building on Phase 7 cache bounds:

| Change | File(s) | Detail |
|--------|---------|--------|
| **Stable compress-cache sharding** | `font/compress_cache.go` | Inline FNV-1a hash (no `hash/fnv` alloc); shard by `fp % shardCount` instead of round-robin; `storePageCompressEntry` uses `LoadOrStore` + proper count |
| **HFT row prealloc retention** | `internal/models/models.go` | `preallocInlineTableRows`: keep `Rows` at len 0 with backing cap; reuse cell slices |
| **Pooled template reuse** | `internal/models/models.go` | `ResetForReuse()` preserves backing arrays across `sync.Pool` reuse |
| **Structure preallocation** | `generator.go`, `structure.go` | `estimateStructureElementCount()` + `ReserveElementCapacity()` at tagged PDF start; shared `growPtrSlice` helper |
| **Alt-string escaping** | `structure.go` | `BeginMarkedContent` / `BeginMarkedContentBuf`: stack-buffer `appendEscapedPDFLiteral` instead of `escapeText()` |

**New tests:** `models_test.go`, `structure_test.go`, cache entry-count assertions in `compress_cache_test.go`.

**k6 2-run mean progression (same harness, same session):**

| Stage | Mean req/s | Δ vs prior |
|-------|----------:|-----------|
| Pre-pass baseline | 916.8 | — |
| Post cache sharding + row prealloc | 989.3 | +7.9% |
| Post pooled template reuse | 1,009.0 | +2.0% |
| Post structure preallocation | **1,025.7** | +1.6% |
| Best single run | **1,052.7** | p99 236.9 ms, HFT avg 323.4 ms |

**Remaining bottlenecks (documented):** `bytes.growSlice` (~50% in-use heap), `compress/flate` (~20% CPU), `drawTable` (~15%), sonic JSON decode (~16% alloc_space). **1,500 req/s gate still open** (~61% of target).

### Phase 8 — PDF validation & XFDF correctness (`4d0b573`, 2026-06-14)

**Commit:** `4d0b573 feat(test): add veraPDF post-test validation and fix XFDF-filled PDF structure`

#### veraPDF post-test gate

- **`test/verify_pdfs.sh`** (486 lines) — parallel veraPDF workers; auto-discover `sampledata/**/generated.*` baselines
- **`test/install_verapdf.sh`** — installer for veraPDF CLI
- **`make test`** now runs Go tests + pytest + veraPDF validation
- New makefile targets: `install-verapdf`, `test-verify-pdfs`, `test-scan-pdfs`
- Editor outputs require **PDF/A-4** and **PDF/UA-2** compliance; htmltopdf/htmltoimg skip size checks (live HTML variance)
- `financialreport/financial_report.json`: `pdfaCompliant: false` — validated as normal PDF, not PDF/A

#### XFDF startxref fix (`internal/pdf/form/xfdf.go`)

- **`setAcroFormNeedAppearancesTrue`** extracted; called **before** xref/trailer write (was after — broke `startxref`)
- **`repairStartxref`**: for object-stream-only fills, rewrites trailer offset to point at XRef stream or `xref` table
- New regex `reXRefStreamObj` for xref stream detection
- Early return path for no-op fills now returns `repairStartxref(out)` instead of raw bytes
- Regression tests: `xfdf_hospital_test.go`, `xfdf_compressed_test.go` assert startxref points at xref table or xref stream

### Phase 9 — Cross-stack benchmark validation (`d50dfd3`, 2026-06-15)

**Source:** `guides/BENCHMARK_COMPARISON_2026-06-15.md`  
**Machine:** WSL2, Intel i7-13700HX, 24 logical CPUs, Go 1.26.4

| Category | Winner | Throughput (validated) |
|----------|--------|------------------------|
| Zerodha weighted (80/15/5, 5000 iter) | GoPDFLib | **2,646 avg / 2,898 peak ops/s** |
| Zerodha retail (48 workers) | GoPDFSuit | **1,978 avg / 2,234 peak ops/s** |
| Data table (2000 rows) | GoPDFLib | **189 ops/s** (92× vs FPDF2) |
| HTTP weighted (48 VUs × 35s) | gopdfsuit | **910 avg / 973 peak req/s** |
| vs Gotenberg | gopdfsuit | **89× faster** (910 vs 10 req/s) |
| pypdfsuit weighted | pypdfsuit | **223 ops/s** |
| Handler micro-bench | `FinancialReport_Parallel` | **~16,669 ops/s** |
| PDF micro-bench (`Rows2000`) | `GenerateTemplatePDF` | **~65 ops/s**, ~15.3M ns/op |

Also added Gotenberg benchmark harness (`18d6137`) and removed duplicate Zerodha benchmarks (`72aee02`) in favor of makefile targets.

### Phase 10 — Release v6, docs, and CI hardening (`925a691` → `dd69309`, 2026-06-15–16)

#### v6.0.0 release prep (`925a691`)

- Go module path: `gopdfsuit/v5` → **`gopdfsuit/v6`**
- pypdfsuit version: **5.0.0 → 6.0.0**
- App `VERSION ?= 6.0.0`
- Removed committed `bin/gopdfsuit` binary (~39 MB)
- Added `guides/release-prep.md` checklist

#### Contributor docs & lint (`ea1d53c`)

- **`CONTRIBUTING.md`** (223 lines): prerequisites (Go 1.26.4, Make, Chrome, Java for veraPDF), workflow, testing layers, branch naming, PR checklist
- **README:** explicit Go **1.26.4** requirement; WSL guidance for Windows
- Lint fixes: `draw.go` goconst nolint; `generator.go` errcheck helpers + removed dead `structElemBuilderPool`; `compress_cache.go` trailing newline

#### CI backend-test job (`66cddfb`, `9d2cbf1`, `5794db0`, `fd7a927`, `dd69309`)

- New **`backend-test`** CI job: Go 1.26.4, Python 3.12, Java 11, veraPDF install, `make test`
- Runs on PRs, branch pushes (non-tag), and manual `full-ci` dispatch
- `build-and-commit-frontend` now **depends on** `backend-test`
- CI installs `fonts-liberation`, `fonts-dejavu-core`, `fonts-noto-core` for PDF/A font consistency
- Integration test `SetupSuite`: calls `font.GetPDFAFontManager().EnsureFontsAvailable()`
- Editor PDF size tolerance harmonized to **8192 bytes** across Go, Python, and veraPDF scripts (was 1024; accounts for PDF/A font embedding + PKCS#7 signature variance in CI)
- Python test fixes: pytest `pythonpath`, Chrome sandbox skip for HTML tests, run from `bindings/python/`

---

## Major code areas changed

| Area | Files | Changes |
|------|-------|---------|
| PDF generation | `internal/pdf/generator.go`, `draw.go`, `structure.go`, `pagemanager.go`, `image.go` | Buffer pooling, compression pipeline, structure tree, table fast paths, cache bounds |
| Fonts & compression | `internal/pdf/font/*.go` | Registry defer removal, flate pool, compress cache sharding, subset cache bounds |
| Caches & utils | `internal/pdf/utils.go`, `image.go`, `font/subset_cache.go` | Bounded props/image/subset caches with clear-on-overflow |
| Handlers | `internal/handlers/handlers.go`, `json_decode.go`, `hft_decode.go` | Sonic pretouch, tier decode, borrowed PDF response |
| Models | `internal/models/models.go` | HFT row prealloc retention, pooled template `ResetForReuse()` |
| XFDF / forms | `internal/pdf/form/xfdf.go` | NeedAppearances before xref; `repairStartxref` for object streams |
| Signing | `internal/pdf/signature/signature.go` | ECDSA support, PEM/signer cache, in-place embed |
| Server | `cmd/gopdfsuit/main.go` | `MAX_CONCURRENT`, pool warmup, fast API mode |
| Test validation | `test/verify_pdfs.sh`, `test/install_verapdf.sh` | veraPDF post-test gate wired into `make test` |
| Benchmarks | `sampledata/benchmarks/gopdfkit_compare/`, `sampledata/gopdflib/zerodha/`, `test/generate_template-pdf/` | Compare harness, k6 load tests, pprof runners, Gotenberg compare |
| CI | `.github/workflows/frontend-build-commit.yml` | `backend-test` job, font packages, veraPDF |
| Tooling | `makefile` | `load-pprof`, `load-pprof-gate`, `load-pprof-1k`, `load-pprof-1500`, `install-verapdf`, `test-verify-pdfs` |
| Go upgrade | `go.mod`, bindings | **Go 1.26.4** across module, Python CGO, CI |
| Release | all `*.go` imports, `pyproject.toml` | **v6.0.0** module path bump |

---

## Reverted or removed experiments

Documented explicitly to avoid re-introducing regressions:

| Experiment | Outcome | Source |
|------------|---------|--------|
| Phase 12 CRC32 + in-place sig hex (Gin) | Reverted — CPU win, no E2E throughput gain | `20260611_gin_1500_ops_pprof_report.md` |
| Store-uncompressed pages ≥96 KiB (Gin) | Reverted — 810 req/s, larger PDFs | same |
| G3 parallel structure-tree build (Zerodha) | Reverted — ~970 ops/s vs ~2,500 | `20260611_zerodha_3000_ops_pprof_report.md` |
| G4 template PDF cache (Zerodha) | Removed — each request must produce unique PDF | same |
| `ReserveMCIDs` ParentTree pre-grow | Fixed (F1) — was 328 MB alloc regression | same |
| HI-3 aggressive buffer/pool caps (8 MB / 1 MB) | Reverted — 993 → 962 req/s, heap growth | `20260614_remaining_optimizations_checklist.md` |
| MI-1 generic structure writer | Reverted — 998 → 916 req/s | same |
| EW-2 compress-cache pre-store `Load` check | Reverted — 808 req/s single run | same |

---

## Verification

```bash
# Internal PDF micro-benchmarks (go1.26.4)
GOCACHE=/tmp/go1264-bench go1.26.4 test ./internal/pdf -run '^$' \
  -bench 'BenchmarkGoPdfSuit|BenchmarkGenerateTemplatePDF' -benchmem -benchtime=5s

# GoPDFKit comparison (fixed harness)
cd sampledata/benchmarks/gopdfkit_compare
GOCACHE=/tmp/go1264-bench go1.26.4 test -run '^$' \
  -bench 'BenchmarkGoPDF(Kit|Lib)$' -benchmem -benchtime=5s

```

items.title: test: measure persistence resource behavior on the qualified platform
items.body:
Closes #326

Companion docs PR: yogeshprasad098/falryn-docs#30 (merge first).

## What changed

[#11](https://github.com/yogeshprasad098/falryn/issues/11) group 5.1 requires
six quantities be *measured on the qualified platform rather than asserted*, and
nothing in the tree measured any of them. This adds the measurement.

- **`src/data/measurement.test.ts`** — a gated module measuring transaction
  latency, busy wait and refusal rate, migration time, database size, artifact
  throughput, and range-read latency against the real owners. It prints each
  result with the five qualifiers `development/TESTING-AND-QUALITY.md` requires:
  hardware/platform, dataset, cold/warm state, sample count, and variability.
- **`package.json`** — `"measure": "FALRYN_MEASURE=1 bun test src/data/measurement.test.ts"`,
  deliberately part of neither `check` nor `ci`.
- **`README.md`** — the command list gains `bun run measure`.
- **`CURRENT-STATE.md`** — the numbers, and what remains unmeasured.

No production source changed. The module is not reachable from `src/main.ts`,
so it never enters the compiled executable.

## Measured on 2026-08-01

macOS 26.6 (`darwin arm64 25.6.0`), Apple M3, 8 logical cores, 16 GiB RAM, Bun
1.3.14. Dataset: 50 sessions of 5 turns — each turn carrying a model attempt, an
invocation, and 4 events, so 1,800 rows of which 1,000 are events — plus 8 MiB
artifacts and 64 KiB range reads.

| Quantity | State | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| transaction latency | warm | 250 samples; median 0.027 ms, p95 0.039 ms, max 2.639 ms |
| busy wait | warm | 5 samples against a 300 ms hold at a 5,000 ms timeout; median 301.911 ms; refused 0/5 |
| refusal rate | warm | 5 samples against a 2,000 ms hold at a 300 ms timeout; refused 5/5 as `busy`, effect `none` |
| migration time | cold | 5 samples on 5 fresh roots; median 2.283 ms, p95 5.602 ms |
| database size | cold | 868,352 bytes (0.83 MiB) for 1,800 rows, no `-wal` or `-shm` |
| artifact throughput | cold and warm | 3 samples of 8 MiB; median 13.337 ms ≈ 600 MiB/s, including the SHA-256 pass |
| range-read latency | warm | 64 samples of 64 KiB at unaligned offsets; median 0.058 ms, p95 0.080 ms |

## Decisions worth reviewing

- **The blob store is the host adapter, never the in-memory double.** The
  nearest precedent, `src/data/artifact-store.test.ts`, composes
  `createInMemoryBlobStore()` — correct for testing ingest logic and useless for
  measuring it. A throughput number taken against memory measures RAM and
  reports it as disk, which is a wrong number rather than a partial one.
- **"Busy retries" is restated as busy wait and refusal rate.** Falryn performs
  no application-level retry: `src/data/sqlite-store.ts` reports `busy` and
  returns, and the retry evaluator in `src/domain/retry.ts` is an
  application-layer policy no persistence path routes through. The retrying that
  happens is SQLite's own busy handler, in C, where no counter is reachable.
  Inventing one would be product behavior implemented inside a measurement.
- **Contention is staged by a second process, not an injected error.**
  `bun:sqlite` is synchronous, so a contending write in this process would block
  the only thread and no timer could release the lock. The holder opens through
  `openBunSqlite` rather than the driver, because the driver-import and
  single-`Database` controls in `src/sqlite-boundaries.test.ts` are
  unconditional — they apply to tests too. That is also the more honest staging:
  the writer contended with is a real Falryn connection.
- **No timing threshold is asserted.** What *is* asserted is that the measured
  work happened — rows counted, digests distinct, read-back bytes correct,
  schema at version 3 — so a run that measured nothing cannot report zero and
  look fast. A quantity that cannot be measured is reported as unmeasured with
  its reason and fails the run, never omitted and never reported as zero.
- **Placement.** A test file inside `src/data/` is exempt from the boundary
  controls that treat a `SqliteStorePort`-naming, SQL-authoring module as a
  defect, is type-checked (a `scripts/` file would not be, given `rootDir` and
  `include`), is linted, and never reaches the compiled binary.

## Divergence from the plan

The issue expected `bun run check` to go from one skip to two. It goes to six:
Bun records each test inside a false `describe.if` as skipped, so this module
contributes five — its four gated tests plus the one explicitly skipped test
that names `bun run measure`. The measurement is visibly absent either way.
`CURRENT-STATE.md` records this.

## Non-goals

A benchmark harness, thresholds, regression detection, or a CI performance job —
[#28](https://github.com/yogeshprasad098/falryn/issues/28), which has no
benchmark child today; that gap is recorded rather than closed by inventing a
sibling. No retry or busy-handling behavior was added. Nothing was tuned: a
number that turns out to be bad is a new issue.

## Validation

```text
bun run check    PASS  (Biome, tsc --noEmit, bun test — 1323 pass, 6 skip, 0 fail)
bun run build    PASS  (Bun standalone executable compiled to dist/falryn)
bun run measure  PASS  (4 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail — all six quantities produced)
```

Re-run at `71c6859`, after the verify corrections below. The table above is that
run; the numbers it replaced were taken at range-read offsets this code no
longer uses.

## Verify corrections (`71c6859`)

Three fixes from the verify of this PR, none changing what is measured.

- **The module header was stale.** It claimed a default `bun run check` reports
  one skipped test from this module; it reports five. The PR body and
  `CURRENT-STATE.md` already said so — the header was the one place left on the
  pre-run expectation.
- **A new Biome warning against baseline.** The generated holder script built its
  error message with a template literal inside a plain string, which reads as a
  template that lost its backticks (`lint/suspicious/noTemplateCurlyInString`).
  It concatenates now, and the branch is back to baseline's single pre-existing
  warning.
- **The range-read byte assertion was weaker than it looked.** Every sampled
  offset was a multiple of the 64 KiB read length, so `bytes[0]` always resolved
  to the same expected value whatever offset was read. The stride is now one byte
  past the read length, so no two samples share a residue mod 256, and both ends
  of each range are checked rather than the first byte alone.

## Documentation impact

| Owner | Impact |
| --- | --- |
| `falryn/CURRENT-STATE.md` | update — the numbers and the remaining limitations |
| `falryn/README.md` | update — the command list gains `bun run measure` |
| `falryn-docs/development/TESTING-AND-QUALITY.md` | update — companion PR #30 |
| `falryn/CONTRIBUTING.md` | verify-unaffected — the measurement is not required before submitting |
| `falryn-docs/operations/PLATFORM-COMPATIBILITY.md` | verify-unaffected — measuring on the qualified platform qualifies no other |

items.title: Compute the docstring examples, reconcile the performance figures, and rename test/ to examples/
items.body:
Three things asked for together, plus the branch cleanup.

## 1. Docstring examples now compute at build time

Every `Examples` block is a `.. jupyter-execute::` directive, following the pattern the sibling Magnus package uses: **self-contained**, importing what it needs, so a block can be copied out of the rendered page and pasted into a session unchanged. The API reference has **0 `>>>` prompts and 42 executed outputs**.

The check that matters: every converted block was run against the output its doctest had documented, and **all 42 reproduce it exactly**. The conversion changed how the examples are *shown*, not what they do.

### The guard did not become hollow

The reason to hesitate over this, raised when it was first proposed, was that `tests/test_docstrings.py` would go on passing while checking nothing — it asserted no doctest *failed*, and no doctests means none failed. So it is repurposed:

- **`test_docstring_examples_run`** extracts and executes the same blocks on every supported Python. The documentation is built by one job on one interpreter; an example that works on 3.12 and not on 3.9 would otherwise reach the published page unnoticed.
- **`test_no_doctests_are_left_behind`** refuses any `>>>` that creeps back, since the first test cannot see one.

Both were checked by breaking them deliberately: an example calling a name that does not exist fails the first, and a restored doctest fails the second with a message naming the module and the count.

## 2. The performance figures are re-measured and reconciled

Three places quoted different numbers for the same four benchmarks, and none matched what the code does now:

| | `fastkernels` | CHANGELOG 1.6.0 | **measured** |
|---|---|---|---|
| 200 000 energies, 3ν | ~20x | 12.5× | **~15x** |
| 20 000 energies, 3ν | ~15x | 15.0× | **~9x** |
| 100×100 oscillogram | ~5x | 2.3× | **~3.5x** |
| 200 000 baselines, 2ν | ~4x | 3.7× | **~1.5x** |

Every live claim — `fastkernels`, README, `index.rst`, `quickstart.rst`, `methodology.rst` — now carries the same measured figures, best of seven with the paths interleaved, and says they move by tens of per cent between runs. The scalar timings had drifted too: **16 µs and 2 µs**, against the 13 and 1.3 previously quoted.

The 1.6.0 changelog entry is left as written. It records what was measured then; rewriting it would falsify the record rather than correct it.

**The structural fix matters more than the numbers.** Three independent copies will drift again, so the documentation now points at [notebook 09](notebooks/09_performance.ipynb), which measures the comparison on whatever machine runs it.

## 3. `test/` is now `examples/`

`test/` and `tests/` held entirely different things and tab-completion could not separate them. Nothing functional depended on the old name: `pytest` never collected from it (`testpaths = ["tests"]`), the scripts locate `src/` relative to themselves, and `git` records all nine files as **renames**, so `--follow` still reaches their history.

The directory is `test/` in v1.0.0 of the code and in v2 of [the paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.12391); the README, installation and quickstart pages say so.

**Two references were reworded rather than renamed**, so they cannot go stale again: the notebooks' shared setup cell explained its `sys.path` line by pointing at the worked examples, and notebook 10 named a directory for plotting modules that no longer exist anywhere.

### Asked first whether `test/` was still used — it is

All nine scripts run, they are what the paper walks through, and the README references them by name. So they stay. But checking surfaced two things:

- **Two were referenced under filenames that do not exist** (`example_*_vacuum_coefficients.py`, where the files are `..._coeffs.py`).
- **Nothing executed them**, which is why that went unnoticed. A step in `lint.yml` now runs all nine, verified to fail when one breaks.

Also caught: the README still described the notebooks as nine; there are fifteen.

## Branch cleanup

`dev-notebooks`, `dev-earth-slabs`, `dev-docs-pass` and `dev-install-pypi` removed from local and remote, each confirmed merged first. `dev_slab` and `dev_time_dep` preserved — both genuinely unmerged.

## Verified

- 355 tests; coverage 100% against the 98% floor
- Sphinx clean under `-W --keep-going`; all 15 notebooks execute and carry figures
- **Each of the five commits passes both the suite and the workflow's own `ruff` command**

One mistake worth recording: the first push failed lint because the rename moved the ruff *per-file-ignores* key and the examples step, but not the linter's own target list. It passed locally because I typed the new path by hand instead of running the workflow's command. The fix was verified by extracting the step from `lint.yml` and running exactly that, and a sweep now confirms every path any workflow step names exists.

items.title: Scrub all docs + CLI help against code; fix surfaced code issues
items.body:
A deep-dive documentation scrub aligning all docs (and CLI help text) with the
current v1.3.0 codebase, plus fixes for the code issues the scrub surfaced.
Every change is backed by reading the actual code; counts are reproducible.

## Documentation (90 docs + 5 CLI source files)
Headline numbers had drifted as the code moved forward:

| Claim | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Patterns | 104 | 158 (teradata 34→84, libraries 16→20) |
| Proto RPCs | 127 | 151 |
| Cataloged models | 44 | 73 |
| Test functions / files | 3,230 / 342 | 3,743 / 397 |

- Rebuilt the provider/model tables from `pkg/llm/catalog/catalog.go` (adds Opus 4.7, GPT‑5.x, Gemini 3.x, Llama 4, etc.).
- Bumped 40 stale `v1.2.0`/beta version badges to v1.3.0 (these aren't managed by the version-manager).
- `pattern-recommendations.md` now carries a complete 138-pattern index.
- `CHANGELOG`/`RELEASE_NOTES` left intact (historical records).

### CLI help-text bugs fixed (help text is documentation)
- `looms` advertised a `looms weave` command family that doesn't exist (stale help-template footer) — removed.
- `looms pattern create/watch --server` defaulted to `localhost:9090` (dead port; server is 60051) — fixed.
- `--llm-provider` help listed 3 of 8 providers; `looms workflow` help said 6 patterns (loader accepts 7); `looms judge` examples used `--judge` (flag is `--judges`); `loom-longmemeval` `download` help said GitHub (it's Hugging Face) and `run --mode` named the wrong default.
- `cli.md` adds `--minimal-tools`; `http-server.md` corrects the LoomService HTTP path count and notes TaskService/SkillsImport are gRPC-only; `task-board.md` drops a non-working HTTP `/v1/boards` example.

## Code fixes surfaced by the scrub
- **fix(config):** empty `observability.mode` was rejected by `Validate()` (defaulted to `service`, required a Hawk endpoint) while the server runs it as `embedded`. Aligned + `-race` test.
- **fix(llm) default models:** OpenAI factory fell back to `gpt-4o` (not in catalog) → `gpt-4.1`; added `huggingface.DefaultHuggingFaceModel` shared by client + factory.
- **docs(proto):** docker `RuntimeType` RUBY/RUST/GO marked reserved (only python/node/custom are implemented).
- **docs(memory):** the salience-engine defaults (0.995/0.05) and agent graph-memory defaults (0.95/0.1) are both intentional and test-pinned; documented the divergence rather than unifying (forcing equality would break tests and change benchmark-validated behavior).

## ⚠️ Behavior change: cost calculators now driven by the catalog
The catalog declares itself the pricing source of truth, but each client's
`calculateCost` had hardcoded drifting rates. Added `catalog.LookupPricing`
(with test) and wired all 6 clients to consult it first, keeping their old
tables only as a fallback for uncataloged ids. **This changes reported cost
numbers** where the catalog differed, e.g.:
- Mistral Large `$2/$6 → $0.50/$1.50`
- Gemini 2.5-pro `$1.875/$12.50 → $1.25/$10`
- OpenAI gpt-5 `$2.50/$10 → $1.25/$10`, o3 `$10/$40 → $2/$8`

Anthropic/Bedrock base rates already matched the catalog (unchanged); Anthropic's cache-token math is preserved on top of the catalog-sourced base rate.

## Verification
- `go build -tags fts5 ./...` (full module) — clean
- `go vet` clean on all changed packages
- `go test -tags fts5 -race` passes for `pkg/llm/...`, `cmd/looms` config, `pkg/memory`
- `gofmt` clean; rebuilt `looms` to confirm help text renders correctly

## Open question for review
`loom-longmemeval --mode` default is `ingest` (help now matches code either way) — confirm `ingest` (vs multi-session) is the intended default.
